## Arbor · One long take per scene — MOSS-Image storyboards + FastH3 OmniRef (MiniMax H3, 8 steps)

A short film of two scenes, each one **continuous 15-second take** with no cuts inside it — the six frames of the scene's storyboard pinned along the way.

1. **Storyboard sheets** holds one prompt per scene (`# Dusk lanterns`, `# Morning after`): each asks for *six panels, three columns and two rows, thin white gutters, no text* and describes every panel. MOSS-Image SFT draws one 3264 × 1216 sheet per scene (4 MP, 50 steps, cfg 3) — one picture keeps the character, light and palette consistent.
2. **Split Grid** cuts every sheet into its six keyframes: one branch per scene, the panels in reading order (the node shows where it cut).
3. Six **List Item** nodes take frame k (index 0 … 5) of **every** scene: their *data* output is one list per frame position — scene 1's frame k, scene 2's frame k. Each list goes into **MiniMax H3 Reference to Video** as `<Picture k>` and into an **Add Guide** that pins it at its frame of the take: 0, 72, 144, 217, 289 and the last (-1). ComfyUI runs the whole chain once per scene.
4. **Prompt Template** (*zip*) writes one structured long-take prompt per scene from a **motion** line (the camera's path through `<Picture 1>` … `<Picture 6>`) and a **sound** line; `{name}` is the scene. 362 frames ≈ 15 s, the longest FastH3 OmniRef is trained for. Keep **Model Sparse Attention** on *vsa* (keep 10 %) and **SigmaShift** at 12 / 3.
5. **Construct Tree** with the scenes as its *structure* names the takes: **Save by Path** files them per scene (`output/arbor/h3_long_takes/0 · Dusk lanterns/000.mp4`), **Video Grid** plays both, **Concatenate Video** joins them into the film — seamless inside each scene, a real cut between scenes.

Why one take per scene: clips pinned only at both ends slow down into every keyframe and stop-and-go at each join; a single take that passes through all six frames keeps moving. More scenes: add a `#` block to all three panels. Not every seed draws a clean grid — check Split Grid's preview and change the seed if panels merge.

nodes.title: Motion · one long take per scene
widgets_values:
# Dusk lanterns
The take opens on <Picture 1>: she stands at the end of the long wooden pier holding an unlit paper sky lantern. The camera glides in along the pier as she strikes a match and lights the lantern, reaching <Picture 2>. It keeps pushing in to a close-up as warm light fills the paper and her face, <Picture 3>. The camera tilts up as she lifts the lantern above her head and lets it go, <Picture 4>. It cranes back behind her as the lantern drifts up to join dozens of others over the lake, <Picture 5>, and keeps rising high above the water as hundreds of lanterns float into the starry sky, <Picture 6>.

# Morning after
The take opens on <Picture 1>: she walks slowly along the misty pier at sunrise, tea steaming in her hand. The camera follows as she sits down at the end of the pier, <Picture 2>, then drifts past her shoulder down to the water, where a burnt-out paper lantern floats beside the pier, <Picture 3>. She leans down and lifts the wet lantern out of the water, <Picture 4>, and the camera rises to her face as she smiles at it in the low sun, <Picture 5>. It cranes back and up as she stands holding the lantern, the sun clearing the mountains and the mist glowing gold, <Picture 6>.

# Dusk lanterns
Water lapping against the pier and a light evening breeze; the scratch and flare of a match and the soft crackle of the flame; a gentle rush of warm air as the lantern rises; wind over the lake and faint distant voices; a soft night breeze and a distant temple bell.

# Morning after
Birdsong over the lake, soft footsteps on wet wood and water lapping gently; a cup set down on the planks; water dripping as the lantern is lifted; a calm morning breeze and distant bells.

nodes.title: Text Encode · one sheet per scene
widgets_values:
A professional anime storyboard sheet: six panels of equal size in a grid of three columns and two rows, each panel a 16:9 frame, separated by thin straight white gutters, no text, no numbers, no captions. One continuous moment at a mountain lake at dusk, the same young woman in a plain deep navy yukata with a red obi and her black hair tied up in every panel, the same wooden pier, the same violet sky.
Panel 1 (top left): wide shot, she stands at the end of the long wooden pier holding an unlit white paper sky lantern.
Panel 2 (top middle): medium shot, she strikes a match and lights the lantern, warm light blooms on her face.
Panel 3 (top right): close-up, the glowing lantern between her hands lights her face from below.
Panel 4 (bottom left): low angle, she releases the lantern above her head, it rises past her fingertips.
Panel 5 (bottom middle): wide shot from behind, she watches her lantern join dozens of lanterns over the lake.
Panel 6 (bottom right): vast wide shot, hundreds of lanterns rise into the starry sky, her small silhouette on the pier.
High-end Japanese anime feature film stills, hand-painted background art, luminous cinematic lighting, consistent character design across all panels
